title: Final: delegates and closures
cards/0/task: Get the output 0 1 2 any way you like.
cards/1/explain: The lambda reads the variable at the moment it is called.
cards/2/explain: Subscribing to a static event without unsubscribing keeps the window in memory forever.
cards/4/q: What does a lambda that captures a local variable create? Select all.
cards/4/options/0: A hidden object for the variable
cards/4/options/3: A copy of the variable on the stack
cards/4/explain: The variable moves into an object on the heap, and the lambda becomes a delegate.
cards/5/q: What does a multicast Func<int> made of two methods return?
cards/5/options/0: The result of the last one
cards/5/explain: To get them all, loop over GetInvocationList().
cards/6/explain: Once you unsubscribe, the event stops holding on to the window.
cards/7/q: Why does for have the closure trap while foreach does not?
cards/7/options/0: Since C# 5 the foreach variable is fresh on each iteration, while for has one for the whole loop
cards/7/explain: The C# 5 change was technically breaking, but everyone saw it as a fix.
